environment.description: Same Go binary deployed on a hardened Kubernetes pod with a custom OCI runtime seccomp profile loaded via RuntimeDefault+ annotation. The profile is derived from the CIS Docker Benchmark Level 2 baseline but further restricts the syscall allowlist to only: read, write, close, fstat, mmap, mprotect, munmap, brk, rt_sigaction, rt_sigprocmask, rt_sigreturn, ioctl, pread64, pwrite64, writev, access, pipe, select, sched_yield, mremap, madvise, nanosleep, getpid, clone, uname, fcntl, flock, fsync, fdatasync, ftruncate, getdents64, getcwd, chdir, openat, newfstatat, lseek, geteuid, getegid, getuid, getgid, arch_prctl, futex, set_tid_address, set_robust_list, clock_gettime, epoll_create1, epoll_ctl, epoll_pwait, eventfd2, accept4, bind, listen, getsockname, getpeername, setsockopt, getsockopt, connect (AF_UNIX only via BPF filter on socket args), tgkill, exit_group, exit. Notably ABSENT from allowlist: execve, execveat, socket (raw creation blocked - only inherited descriptors from runtime bootstrap permitted via SCM_RIGHTS), ptrace, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev, fork, vfork, clone3. The profile is enforced via Seccomp type: Localhost with the JSON profile mounted from a read-only ConfigMap at /etc/seccomp/restricted-nosql-svc.json. Additionally, the pod runs with allowPrivilegeEscalation: false and capabilities dropped to empty set.
